scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8871: host_2_1_1_1 (10.2.1.2) reports it has lost everything
beyond its own gateway: every 10.200.0.x server times out, and it cannot reach
host_1_1_1_1 in the other pod either. It CAN still ping its gateway 10.2.1.1.
Pod 1 is unaffected -- host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm normally. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on router_core_2 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_2 ospfd
Mechanism: router_core_2 is pod 2's only way out: switch_dist_2_1's single
  uplink (172.16.0.8/31, area 1) terminates on router_core_2, which as the
  pod-2 ABR carries 10.2.1.0/24 between area 1 and the area-0 backbone. With
  ospfd killed, zebra flushes router_core_2's OSPF routes immediately, so
  pod-2 traffic arriving at router_core_2 has no route and dies there; the
  other routers then age out router_core_2's LSAs and withdraw 10.2.1.0/24.
  Pod 1 (host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> router_core_3 -> farm)
  never transits router_core_2, so it stays healthy.
Localization: router_core_2
Root cause: ospfd not running on router_core_2
Fix: restart FRR on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on router_core_2" -- that is the same fault observed at the
config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).
Unlike the vtysh-provisioned Kath labs, this topology keeps its OSPF config
in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process, not the file), so a
plain restart reloads the full configuration, OSPF re-converges, and pod 2
regains connectivity.
scoring_axes: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2

agent.diagnosis_text:
The ospfd process on router_core_2 crashed approximately 42 seconds after lab
startup and has not been restarted. FRR logs confirm the sequence: ospfd loaded
its configuration correctly at 09:24:54, briefly completed OSPF DD negotiation
with router_core_1 (neighbour 172.16.0.0) at 09:25:43, then Zebra reported
"Client 'ospf' (session id 0) encountered an error and is shutting down" at
09:26:25, immediately withdrawing all 9 OSPF routes from the kernel RIB. The
current process table on router_core_2 shows only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd —
ospfd is absent. Crucially, watchfrr is also not running, so the crash was
permanent rather than self-healing.

Without ospfd, router_core_2 has no OSPF routes: its RIB contains only its
three directly connected /31 transit links. switch_dist_2_1 (pod-2 distribution
layer) peers with router_core_2 over 172.16.0.8/31 and likewise has no routes
beyond its directly connected segments. As a result, any traffic from
host_2_1_1_1 that reaches its gateway (10.2.1.1 on switch_dist_2_1) is
black-holed at router_core_2 for all non-local destinations — the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm and the 10.1.1.0/24 pod-1 subnet alike. Pod 1 is unaffected because
router_core_1 is healthy and retains a full OSPF table.

Root cause: ospfd on router_core_2 was killed or crashed post-startup with
watchfrr also absent, leaving the router permanently without OSPF.

Corrective fix: Restart ospfd on router_core_2 (e.g., `service frr restart` or
`/usr/lib/frr/ospfd -d -F traditional -A 127.0.0.1`). Also ensure watchfrr is
running (`/usr/lib/frr/watchfrr -d zebra mgmtd staticd ospfd`) so future ospfd
crashes trigger automatic recovery.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies router_core_2 as the affected device and attributes the ospfd crash and missing routes to it.
The agent explicitly states ospfd on router_core_2 crashed/was killed and is absent from the process table, identifying the OSPF daemon as down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis notes Pod 1 is unaffected but does not confirm the server farm stays healthy—in fact it contradictorily claims the server farm is black-holed—so it fails to isolate the fault solely to Pod 2's transit through router_core_2.
Recommends restarting ospfd/FRR (e.g., service frr restart) and enabling watchfrr for automatic recovery, which matches the expected corrective fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (process list, routing table snippets, FRR logs) that support the diagnosis that ospfd crashed on router_core_2 and was not restarted; the causal chain from crash → route withdrawal → pod-2 blackhole is logical and well-supported, and the checks cover the required surfaces. Minor truncation of some command outputs is present but does not undermine the core evidence.
